title: FY2025 Financial Snapshot
subtitle: Key figures and drivers for the fiscal year ending 31 March 2025

overview.text: The company reported revenue of INR 250 crore in FY2025, up from INR 220 crore in FY2024. This indicates growth in top-line sales over the prior year. Profit after tax for FY2025 was INR 18 crore. The financial position as of 31 March 2025 shows borrowings of INR 65 crore and receivables of INR 92 crore. All amounts are denominated in Indian Rupees (INR) and measured in crores (1 crore equals 10 million).

The increase in receivables is attributed to customer payment delays. This suggests that while revenue grew, cash collection faced headwinds, leading to a higher balance of money owed to the company. The document explicitly states that these figures must not be relabelled as USD or converted into millions, preserving the original INR crore units.

highlights.text: Revenue increased from INR 220 crore in FY2024 to INR 250 crore in FY2025.
Profit after tax stood at INR 18 crore in FY2025.
Borrowings were recorded at INR 65 crore as of 31 March 2025.
Receivables reached INR 92 crore, driven by customer payment delays.

risks.text: Customer payment delays have increased receivables, which may impact cash flow and working capital efficiency.
The presence of INR 65 crore in borrowings indicates debt obligations that require servicing.

questions: What specific measures are being taken to address customer payment delays?
How does the INR 65 crore in borrowings affect the company's debt service coverage?
Are there any changes in credit policies that contributed to the increase in receivables?
